hero.about: Close-up renders and printing. Keeps the full detail, tidied and with its materials baked so a GLB carries them.

quads.about: Keep modeling it. Clean quads in regular loops, denser where the shape curves, ready to edit or subdivide.

web.about: Web pages and product viewers. Adaptive quads, 1024 textures with a normal map, compressed.

game.about: Real-time games. A few thousand adaptive quads; the normal map carries the fine detail. WebP textures and Draco compression keep the download small.

mobile.about: Phones and AR. As light as it gets while keeping the silhouette.

midpoly.about: Phone games on today's hardware: the same simple pieces as the low-poly version, built again rounder and smooth, a few thousand triangles, with the detailed mesh's color, bumps and shine baked on. Gear still comes off.

lowpoly.about: Old-school real-time style, like early Warcraft: a few hundred triangles Claude blocks out from simple shapes, with the detail's color and soft shadows painted into one small texture.

flat_colors.about: Old-school real-time style with flat colors (think old RuneScape): Claude's block-out with one color per part and faceted shading, no texture at all.

painted.about: The mid-poly character on the wardrobe's shared body, its own head kept, with its skin-tight clothes (the gear its wardrobe.json names: a singlet, tights, an undershirt) painted into the body's texture instead of worn as meshes. Painted cloth cannot be poked through by the skin and costs no triangles, and an outfit painted for one character fits any other. Loose clothes, boots and anything whose outline matters keep their meshes.

walk.about: The same character with a skeleton and a walk of its own: bones placed from its build, joints that stop where a body's do, and a looping walk worked out from its leg length, bulk and manner. Gear and prop points follow the bones.

run.about: The same character with its skeleton and a looping run on the spot. The run comes from one sentence about how this character runs, made into motion by NVIDIA Kimodo and cut where two strides match; its feet stay planted, its joints stay inside their limits, and loose cloth swings at running speed. Made only when the run clip is there (just runs).

rom.about: The same character with its skeleton, going through a range-of-motion routine standing in place: arms overhead, a twist and a side bend each way, a bend forward, a squat, a punch with each hand. For checking what skin, clothes and joints do when the body is pushed further than a walk pushes it; not shown in the gallery.

sides.about: The same character with its skeleton, playing the audition sides standing in place: standing easy, a wave, a head turn each way, the right arm raised overhead, a deep squat held. The same scenes for everyone trying out for a part (scripts/casting), chosen for what a walk never asks of the knees, shoulders and neck.
